Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the EcoNova Energy Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, please press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, please press star then two. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss EcoNova Energy's results for the Q3 2024. Joining me on today's call are Sarah Chen, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Torres, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Development Officer; Dr. Raj Singh, Chief Technology Officer; Elena Vasquez, Chief Sustainability Officer; and Tom Reilly, Chief Operating Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements. We encourage you to review the disclaimer in our press release and on our website regarding these statements.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Sarah Chen.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. EcoNova Energy delivered exceptional results in the Q3 2024, showcasing our leadership in the renewable energy sector. Our success is attributable to our innovative technologies, strategic partnerships, and unwavering commitment to sustainability.

Today, I want to highlight seven key aspects of our performance:

1. The significant impact of government incentives and subsidies propelling our growth.
2. Outstanding capacity factor performance across our solar, wind, and storage technologies.
3. A favorable policy and regulatory environment accelerating deployments.
4. New power purchase agreements secured with strong average pricing.
5. Effective capital recycling through asset sale transactions.
6. Disciplined capital expenditure and operating expense management.
7. Robust revenue and earnings growth driven by volume and efficiency.

Now, I'll hand over the call to Michael Torres to provide a detailed review of our financial results.

Michael Torres:
Thank you, Sarah. Our financial performance in the Q3 2024 was outstanding. Revenue reached $1.8 billion, representing a 22% increase compared to the same period last year. This growth was driven by significant project commissioning and increased energy production. Our gross margin expanded to 32.5%, reflecting improved operational efficiency and cost management. Operating expenses totaled $450 million, primarily due to investments in R&D and sales and marketing. Net income was $300 million, or $1.45 per share. We ended the quarter with $1.2 billion in cash and cash equivalents. We are raising our full-year guidance for revenue and earnings.

Before we move on, let me expand on some of these drivers, starting with the critical role of government incentives and subsidies. As a leader in utility-scale solar PV, onshore wind, and battery energy storage systems, we've long benefited from these policies, which de-risk our projects and accelerate deployment at scale. In Q3 alone, incentives underpinned approximately 28% of our adjusted EBITDA, up from 22% in the prior-year period, reflecting favorable policy tailwinds and our strategic positioning.

In the United States, the Inflation Reduction Act continues to be a game-changer, with its uncapped Investment Tax Credit and Production Tax Credit extensions driving outsized returns. For solar and wind, the base 30% ITC—stackable with bonuses for domestic content up to 10%, energy communities at 10%, and low-income areas at 10-20%—delivered an effective credit value of 45-55% on eligible capital expenditures this quarter. Our 1.2 GW Gemini Solar + Storage project in Nevada qualified for the full 50% adder, generating $185 million in transferable tax credits monetized via our partnership with JPMorgan's tax equity syndicate at a 92% realization rate.

On storage, the standalone 30% ITC for BESS has been transformative. Our 850 MW portfolio additions, including the 300 MW/1,200 MWh standalone system co-located with Texas wind farms, benefited from this, reducing our weighted average cost of capital by 120 basis points to 5.8%. Clean hydrogen under the 45V PTC, yielding up to $3 per kg, is gaining traction; our pilot 10 MW electrolyzer at the Port of Long Beach secured a provisional $22 million from the DOE's Regional Clean Hydrogen Hubs program.

Year-to-date, IRA-related benefits have contributed $420 million to free cash flow, 35% of total FCF, enabling a 15% YoY increase in our development pipeline to 18 GW. Our Nevada Gigafactory ramp-up to 5 GW annual module capacity unlocked $50 million in domestic content bonuses, mitigating future phase-outs of Section 45X credits.

In Europe, with 4.5 GW across Germany, Spain, and the UK, subsidies have shifted from Feed-in Tariffs to auctions and merchant exposure. Germany's EEG reforms and the €200 billion REPowerEU plan sustained high CfD strike prices—averaging €55/MWh for our 500 MW Spanish bifacial PV portfolio—yielding IRRs over 9%. Our Orsted-partnered 400 MW onshore wind in the North Sea got a 15-year CfD at €49/MWh, plus a €32 million EU Innovation Fund grant for Haliade-X hybrids.

Subsidy cliffs are ahead, like the UK's CfD Round 6 at £37/MWh, down 18% YoY, but we've diversified 20% into merchant markets where LCOE at $25/MWh for solar beats new gas, maintaining 7.5% blended yields with TSO curtailment revenues.

In Asia-Pacific, India's PLI scheme slashed module costs 22% on our 2 GW Rajasthan project with a ₹4,500 crore allocation, uplifting IRR by 12%. Australia's CIS covered 40% of capex on our 450 MW South Australia BESS, hitting AUD 120/MWh LCOS. Our China JV with LONGi leverages the Golden Sun program for 15% QoQ export growth.

Overall, incentives drove our 22% revenue lift and 450 bps gross margin expansion, with global subsidies at $1.3 trillion in 2023 and more coming. We're hedging with 40% unsubsidized PPAs by 2026 via hyperscalers prioritizing 24/7 carbon-free power, while lobbying for PTC/ITC permanence. Risks like policy reversals could hit 15-20% of credits, but we expect 25-30% of 2025 EBITDA from this.

Turning to capacity factor performance, our fleet-wide blended came in at 32.4%, up 180 bps YoY, reflecting yield optimization. For solar PV, our 4.2 GW portfolio hit 27.2%, beating NREL's 24.8% benchmark. California assets like 500 MW Forge Valley reached 28.9% with bifacial PERC and 6.8 kWh/m²/day irradiance; Texas at 25.4% despite curtailment, aided by single-axis trackers on 60% of builds boosting yield 20-25%. We're piloting AI soiling mitigation for 1-2% uplift.

Wind onshore at 38.7%, offshore 51.2%. Iowa Plains' 400 MW hit 41.2% with Vestas V150s; offshore North Sea at 51.2% via Siemens Gamesa SG 14-222 DD. WindBoost CFD layouts cut losses 4%, Predix maintenance slashed downtime 25%.

Storage utilization at 22.6%, with ERCOT's Longhorn at 28.4% on arbitrage, California at 19.8% with Fluence EMS, Europe at 24.1%. Second-life batteries cut capex 15%, RTE 92.3%. Storage contributes 35% EBITDA at 60% margins, scaling to 5 GW/20 GWh.

On revenue and earnings growth, we hit $1.28 billion revenue in recent quarters, but Q3's $1.8 billion reflects 48% YoY acceleration from volume, pricing, and tailwinds. Adjusted EBITDA $285 million up 52%, margins 22.3%. Solar $665 million +55%, wind $358 million +42%, storage $192 million +68%, clean tech $64 million +35%. North America 62%, Europe 25%, APAC 13%. Supply chain drops, R&D breakthroughs like AI controls adding $25 million EBITDA, Verdant acquisition fuel this. Raised FY24 to $5.4-5.6 billion.

For new PPAs, we secured 1.2 GW across five projects, backlog to 4.8 GW. Arizona's 450 MWdc Rattlesnake +200 MW storage at $38/MWh with APS; Texas 250 MW hybrid with TechColossus at $42/MWh; New York 150 MW at $52/MWh. Average new PPA $41/MWh, up 5% YoY, backlog $39/MWh. Hybridization, laddering, merchant clauses drive pricing power; guide 1.5-2 GW more at $42-44/MWh.

Capital recycling: $2.8 billion in sales TTM, recycling 28% capex. 750 MW wind to Brookfield/OMERS at $1.93 million/MW; 450 MW solar+BESS to BlackRock at $2.67 million/MW. Proceeds into 1.2 GW floating wind, 800 MW solar. $4.5 billion pipeline for 2025-26.

CAPEX Q3 $452 million, up 28% YoY: solar $235 million at $0.92/Wdc, wind $127 million at $1.1 million/MW, BESS $68 million at $220/kWh. OPEX $185 million: O&M $89 million, SG&A $59 million. Intensity down, guidance $1.8-2.0 billion CAPEX.

I'll now turn the call over to Lisa Patel to discuss our project development activities.

Lisa Patel:
Thank you, Michael. Our project development pipeline continues to expand, with 18 GW of projects under development across various renewable energy technologies. We are making excellent progress on securing land rights, obtaining permits, and negotiating power purchase agreements. We expect to bring several new projects online in the coming quarters, further contributing to our revenue and profitability. We are also actively pursuing strategic acquisitions and partnerships to accelerate our growth. On the policy front, the outlook remains a powerful tailwind. In the US, IRA unlocked $1.2 billion in benefits for our 5 GW pipeline; state SGIP boosted storage 40%. FERC reforms could cut queues 12-18 months. Europe's REPowerEU hit 47% renewables mix; our Dutch wind CfD at €62/MWh. UK's reforms sped approvals 30%. Asia's China prices down 45%, India's PM Surya Ghar added $150 million. Corporate PPAs 28% of additions, carbon pricing covers 24% GDP. Our backlog $28 billion, 85% contracted.

Dr. Raj Singh, can you update us on our technological advancements?

Dr. Raj Singh:
Thank you, Lisa. We are dedicated to driving innovation in the renewable energy sector. Our R&D efforts are focused on developing advanced technologies that enhance the efficiency, reliability, and affordability of renewable energy systems. We have made significant breakthroughs in areas such as advanced solar panel technologies, energy storage solutions, and smart grid technologies. We believe that these technologies will play a pivotal role in transforming the energy landscape.

Next, Elena Vasquez will discuss our sustainability initiatives.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Dr. Singh. Sustainability is a core value at EcoNova Energy, and we are committed to minimizing our environmental impact and contributing to a more sustainable future. We have established ambitious goals for reducing our carbon emissions, improving our energy efficiency, and promoting responsible resource management. We are also actively involved in community engagement and supporting local initiatives that advance sustainability.

Now, Tom Reilly will provide operational highlights.

Tom Reilly:
Thank you, Elena. Our operational performance remains strong. We are focused on optimizing our operations, improving efficiency, and ensuring the reliability of our renewable energy assets. We are implementing best practices in areas such as asset management, maintenance, and supply chain management. We are also investing in training and development to ensure that our employees have the skills and knowledge they need to succeed.

I'll turn it back to Sarah Chen for closing remarks.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Tom. To summarize, EcoNova Energy had an exceptional Q3 2024. We are confident that our strategic initiatives, our commitment to innovation, and our focus on sustainability will drive continued growth and success.

Operator, let's proceed with the Q&A session.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, at this time we will begin the question-and-answer session. Please limit yourself to one question and one follow-up. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
What are your plans for expanding your presence in international markets?

Sarah Chen:
Thanks, John. International expansion is a key pillar of our growth strategy. We're prioritizing high-resource regimes like Europe and APAC, where we've grown to 4.5 GW operating and 15 GW pipeline. In Europe, REPowerEU and CfDs support our Dutch and Spanish builds; in India and Australia, PLI and CIS incentives align with our hybrids. We'll deploy $500 million from recycling into 2 GW international CODs by 2026, targeting 30% of revenue from non-US by FY26, hedged via long-term PPAs.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Maria Lopez with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Maria Lopez:
How are you addressing the challenge of intermittency associated with renewable energy sources?

Dr. Raj Singh:
Great question, Maria. Intermittency is core to our innovation focus. Our 2 GW/8 GWh BESS co-locates with 70% solar, delivering 22.6% utilization via arbitrage and services. Fluence EMS and ML forecasting optimize cycles; hybrids like Rattlesnake boost capture 20-25%. Long-duration pilots with Form Energy and hydrogen stacking target firming for hyperscalers' 24/7 CFP. Capacity factors—solar 27.2%, wind offshore 51.2%—plus WindBoost layouts minimize variability.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Kim with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

David Kim:
Can you discuss the impact of government subsidies and tax incentives on your profitability?

Michael Torres:
Absolutely, David. Subsidies drove 28% of Q3 EBITDA, up from 22%, via IRA ITC/PTC at 45-55% effective. Gemini's $185 million credits monetized at 92%; storage WACC down 120 bps. YTD $420 million FCF boost. Europe CfDs at €55/MWh yield 9% IRRs; India PLI 12% uplift. Gross margins +450 bps to 32.5%. Hedging to 40% unsubsidized by 2026, but expect 25-30% EBITDA contribution in 2025.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen:
What are your expectations for electricity demand growth in the coming years?

Sarah Chen:
Emily, demand growth is explosive, driven by electrification, EVs, and AI data centers. IEA sees 4% CAGR to 2030, but US hyperscalers alone need 50 GW new capacity yearly. Our 18 GW pipeline, 4.8 GW contracted PPAs at $41/MWh, positions us perfectly. Storage firming and hybrids meet this; corporate PPAs up 30% YoY. We're guiding 25% capacity growth, capturing share in $1.7 trillion capex.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, there appear to be no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back over to Sarah Chen for any closing remarks.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you all for your participation in today's call. We appreciate your continued support of EcoNova Energy. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
